newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Paris stocks, dollar, hit by French poll fears.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Paris stocks, dollar, hit by French poll fears.

text.p: Speculation over a snap French election caused a sharp fall in Paris stocks on Monday and hit the dollar as anxious currency investors turned to the mark.
The U.S. currency slipped nearly a pfennig with the French political uncertainty denting the recent optimism over prospects for Europe's single currency and thus strengthening the mark.
London edged ahead after Wall Street made a positive start and Frankfurt ended floor trade only just in the plus column. But Paris had a bad day, slipping over one percent.

The French bourse was spooked because investors expect President Jacques Chirac to call elections as the government seeks a mandate to push through austerity measures aimed at qualifying France for a single European currency by 1999.
Chirac's gamble could pay off with a fresh mandate but it could also unleash protest votes, perhaps favouring the Socialists or the National Front.

Socialist leader Lionel Jospin on Sunday tempered his enthusiasm for a single currency when he said he would not impose tough policies to hit the three percent Maastricht deficit target if that increased unemployment -- effectively setting out the election agenda. "The strong absolute performance seen (in the stock market) since the beginning of the year could dry up or even reverse," if the political risk increases in the coming weeks, Gary Dugan, equity strategist at JP Morgan said.
Besides stocks, the franc bonds and interest rate contracts all suffered from the mood of political uncertainty, extending last week's losses.
The franc weakened against the German currency, trading at 3.3715 per mark, compared with 3.3698 late on Friday.
In Frankfurt, floor trade was down for much of the day as the dollar's slide against the mark dimmed prospects for the exports sector.

But the market mananged to claw back the losses to finish trading marginally ahead though worries over the consequences of the weaker dollar persisted and after-hours computerised deals were well down.
"If we see another five or ten pfennigs off the dollar, that's going to be really bad news," said a Frankfurt trader. "All this currency talk could bring us pretty much to our knees this week."
Industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG came under the most dollar-driven pressure and was down 2.35 marks at 128.05 marks in afternoon trade.
Dealers said Daimler's problems were exacerbated by a report in the Bild newspaper that Bonn was planning to sharply raise petrol tax. The government denied its plans.

London, Europe's biggest bourse, climbed by 0.25 percent as worries over interest rates and the outcome of the May 1 election were offset by the debut of Britain's newest bank, which surpassed expectations.
Shares in newly-floated Alliance & Leicester began trading at 542.5p before climbing as high as 556p in rapid early trade.
On the currency front the dollar was hit by the stronger mark, benefiting from the EMU worries."The French election speculation has given the mark overall strength," said a Japanese bank dealer.

Analysts said the new bout of jitters over prospects for Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) was because of fears that new government may be less willing to push through austerity measures to meet EMU criteria.
The dollar was also down half a yen and analysts said caution before next weekend's meeting of the G7 industrialised nations in Washington was likely to keep it subdued in the short term.

"The issue of the strong dollar (against the yen) is being linked into the G7 and the risk is for a strongly worded statement. This is keeping things steady and stable for the moment," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered Bank in London.
The G7 meeting on April 27 is after a meeting between Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and U.S. President Bill Clinton on Friday, April 25.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7030 marks and 125.50 yen after ending at 1.7129 and 125.94 in late trading in Europe on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1430 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 10.3 points at 4,320.8.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 28.28 points at 2,519.24.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 3.19 points at 3,347.58.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in the afternoon at $342.25 an ounce versus $342.45 at the close in London on Friday. Silver was three cents higher at $4.76.
